target_customer: Software and IT teams of 1 to 500 people, with a sweet spot of 10 to 100, that run Scrum and agile projects
problem: Scrum teams needed fast project planning, backlog and burndown tracking that non technical stakeholders and vendors could also use.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per plan, sold by Pluron, Inc. doing business as Acunote
product_category: Agile and Scrum project management software

founders.name: Gleb Arshinov
founders.background_notes: YC page and the company page list him as founder and CEO. Alexander Dymo is listed on the company page as Director of Engineering and first company employee, not as a founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web based Scrum planning tool with real time updates and a Gmail style interface was standard web engineering, with a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Teams keep their backlog and history in the tool, but many agile tools existed and no unique data or network effect is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pivotal Labs was bought by EMC in March 2012. No source shows Acunote being acquired or copied, and the site is still selling plans in 2026.

market_need_then: Acunote was a profitable small business before YC according to its own July 2012 blog post, with customers such as IBM, Fujitsu, VMware, HP, EMC and Disney named in TechCrunch. That shows paying demand for agile tooling.

branding.domain_note: Uses acunote.com. No purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: plain product site with pricing and testimonials

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch covered the July 2012 launch. No evidence of merch or community. Legal entity is Pluron, Inc.

brand_strength.rationale: Known to agile practitioners and listed on comparison sites, with no source showing a brand asset or community.

outcome_analysis: Acunote was already a profitable small business before it joined YC in Winter 2011 and formally launched as a YC company in July 2012. No outside funding or exit is documented, and the company still sells subscriptions in 2026 under Pluron, Inc. The record fits a bootstrapped niche software business that stayed small next to better funded agile tools.
notes: Competitors: the TechCrunch launch article of July 2, 2012 names Pivotal Labs (Pivotal Tracker), LiquidPlanner and Asana, but that is about 18 months after the January 2011 batch start, so it is not used for the as of 2011 list. Founding year not stated in sources. Funding not found; the company blog describes a profitable business before YC, which is not proof of zero outside funding. The YC page lists no bios.
